title: Priority gating for high-value account requests
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently receive a stream of high-touch requests from strategic accounts (feature asks, infra changes, compliance asks). Without a standardized, measurable gate these requests either clog the roadmap or are handled ad hoc by SEs and AMs, leading to missed SLAs and misaligned engineering effort.

Goal: Define and implement a lightweight, score-based priority gate and SLA flow for high-value accounts that: 1) ensures consistent Triage and Commitment SLAs for top accounts; 2) surfaces requests into the roadmap queue with clear acceptance criteria; 3) provides observable signals that the GTM, CS, and Eng teams can act on; 4) minimizes false-positive escalations to engineering.

Proposal:
- Implement a scoring model applied at intake that combines: account ARR weight, renewal proximity, strategic partner status, technical-blocker severity, and product-fit alignment. Scores are normalized to a 0-100 scale.
- Define three intake outcomes based on score bands: "Rapid Escalation" (80-100): immediate canary SLAs and engineering review within 5 business days; "Request Queue" (50-79): product review and prioritization in the next planning cycle; "Manage via CS" (<50): handled by CS/SE with SLO'd responses and no roadmap commitment.
- Formalize SLAs: Triage acknowledgment within 24 business hours for band 3 requests, full intake review within 5 business days for band 1, and product-commit/reject decision within one planning cycle or explicit fallback.
- Add an automated tagging and routing rule in the Console intake flow so requests from accounts on "Top Accounts" list are auto-scored and flagged.
- Create dashboard metrics: intake volume by band, time-to-triage, time-to-decision, acceptance rate, and downstream engineering effort hours.
- Rollout plan: 1) pilot with top-10 strategic accounts for 6 weeks; 2) collect feedback and refine scoring weights; 3) expand to top-50 accounts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict scoring reduces noise but risks rejecting nuanced asks — mitigation: manual override by Solutions Engineering with mandatory justification.
- Fast SLAs increase operational load — mitigation: cap number of "Rapid Escalation" slots per cycle and use a quota with rollover.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: deep automation of the scoring algorithm via ML, changes to Contract/Legal terms for SLAs, and building new UI surfaces beyond intake tagging and dashboard widgets.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring model documented and published in Confluence with weight definitions and examples
Console intake flow tags requests from accounts on the Top Accounts list and computes initial score
Routing rules created: auto-notify PM/SE/Eng leads for "Rapid Escalation" band requests
SLA paths defined and visible in intake tickets: triage ack within 24 business hours (band 3) and full review window of 5 business days (band 1)
Dashboard created showing intake volume by band, time-to-triage, time-to-decision, and acceptance rate
Pilot run completed with top-10 accounts and retrospective notes captured
Manual override workflow implemented with audit trail and required justification
notes: Scoring candidate features: ARR (40%), renewal window (20%), strategic partner flag (15%), technical severity (15%), product-fit score (10%)
Quota for Rapid Escalations: default 3 slots per cycle (configurable per PM), slots consumed are visible to CS/AMs
Fallback policy: if engineering capacity prevents commitment within SLA, automatic downgrade to Request Queue and customer notified with next-steps
Security review not required for intake gating itself, but specific requests may trigger security_review_required flag
We will use existing Top Accounts list maintained by GTM; ownership: Head of Customer Success to keep list current
